about: The correct answers to the questions the AI answers demo asks (examples/specs/ai-answers.spec.json), each with why. A question is its page, the AI's check and the scanner's target. examples/ai-demo-score.js compares a run with them.

answers.why: The title is "Page": it does not say what the page is about (garden tools).
The alt text is a file name, IMG_2041.jpg.
"Canvas garden bag with two leather handles" describes the picture of the garden bag it sits with.
The image says −50%, which the text beside it ("on all seeds this week") does not: it carries meaning, so alt="" hides it.
A thin grey line between sections: decorative.
"Plan of the garden" says what the picture of the image map is; its areas name the parts.
The area over the greenhouse, linking to it, is named "Greenhouse".
The area over the tool shed is named "Area 2", a placeholder that says nothing of where it leads.
An image button showing "Check" in the delivery form, named "Check delivery": it says what the button does.
The same button named "btn_submit_02.png", a file name.
alt="" with the name "button" from aria-label: a placeholder, not what the button does.
A bar chart of seeds sold in January, February and March, March the highest; its fallback text says just that.
The garden plan embedded with the title "garden-plan.svg": its file name, which says nothing of what it shows.
A canvas drawing the weather (a sun and a cloud) named "canvas", with fallback text that only says canvas is not supported.
A shopping cart icon with alt "Cart": accurate for what it shows (its repetition of the link text is the redundant-alt question).
The icon's alt "Cart" repeats the link text "Cart" beside it, so "Cart Cart" is read; alt="" would lose nothing.
The video has no name of its own, but its figcaption "How to prune roses (2 minutes)" identifies it.
A magnifying glass, the only content of a link to the products, named "Search products": it says what the link does.
The only content of a button, named by its title "Layer 1", a layer name left over from the drawing tool: it says nothing of what the button does.
"Delivery" in bold heads the paragraph after it: it should be a heading.
"Demo Shop" in the header is the site's name, not the heading of a section.
"Learn more", alone in its paragraph, does not say about what.
Its only label is a title attribute: nothing visible says what to enter.
Its only label is a placeholder, gone as soon as one types.
"Offers - Demo Shop" says what the page is.
The site's name in the header, not a section heading.
Home, Products and Cart show no change at all when focused: their outline is removed and nothing replaces it (Help shows focus from a script).
Home: outline removed, no other change on focus.
Products: outline removed, no other change on focus.
Cart: outline removed, no other change on focus.
No indicator at all: nothing changes on focus.
No indicator at all.
No indicator at all.
Help: its outline is removed, but on focus a script gives it a dark background and white text.
Help: the whole link turns dark on focus, far more than a 2 px line around it, at well over 3:1.
Home: nothing changes on focus, so there is no indicator to meet 3:1.
Products: no indicator.
Cart: no indicator.
Help: dark blue on the white header, far above 3:1.
The last link on the page ("Seeds and bulbs", tabindex="1") comes first, before the navigation.
The account menu and two product tiles react to the mouse but Tab never reaches them.
A click handler on a span that cannot take focus.
role="button" but it cannot take focus.
Once the page has scrolled, the sticky header lies entirely over the Roses and Tulips links while they have focus.
The same links, hidden by the sticky header.
"Demo Shop" in bold is the site name in the header, not a section title.
"Garden gloves - Demo Shop" names the product the page is about and the site.
"Size guide" opens a modal dialog a keyboard user cannot close: its only close control is a span (it cannot take focus) and Escape does nothing (with open: true).
The size guide is a modal dialog (aria-modal), and opening it leaves focus on the link behind it: focus should move into the dialog.
Nothing on the page removes the browser's focus outline: every stop shows focus.
